root.claim: There is one deterministic fixed-alphabet, fixed-tape Turing machine multiplying $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Reduce the product to a digit convolution computed with Fourier-type transforms on power-of-two axes, and accelerate the transforms' address rearrangements and butterfly layers by a power of the logarithm.

motivation.text: Scanning the array at each of the logarithmically many transform levels already costs $n\log n$, so a power saving needs the movement and the arithmetic per level to be cheaper than a scan.

children.method: Build each procedure from a fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values and restores its scratch values, and apply it recursively with a strict rank deficit.

children.claim: Two chunks of $e=m^k$ digits can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time by running a fixed exchange network of $W$ wires whose edges are smaller interchanges, with $s<Wm$ smaller calls in all.
children.method: Exchange the chunks with a shear $H\leftarrow H+D$ run through the bit network on $W$ role streams of volume $V/W$, implement each edge by smaller interchanges, and solve the recursion.

motivation.text: The cost per unit volume is multiplied by $s/W$ at each level; because the sum of ranks $s$ is less than the number of wires times $m$, this multiplier is below $m$ and the recursion saves a power of the chunk width.

children.method: Reduce the product to a cyclic convolution of digit lists on coprime axes and evaluate it by the transform, pointwise product and inverse transform with the retained permutation cancelling.

motivation.text: Splitting into digits turns the product into a convolution, and the convolution theorem turns the convolution into one pointwise product between a transform and its opposite.

children.method: Use the Chinese remainder theorem with coordinate powers $\mu_i=P_i^{-1}$ chosen so that axis $i$ depends only on lower-index digits, which makes the change of order a sequence of controlled shifts.

motivation.text: With these powers the new coordinate $b_i$ is $a_i$ plus a multiple of the lower digits modulo $s_i$, a shift of a later field controlled by earlier fields.
